subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

judge.implied_focus: Incident resolution performance / efficiency (how long and how effectively incidents get resolved)

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: Directly measures the core outcome of resolution performance -- the central quantity of the implied focus.

per_column.name: is_critical
per_column.rationale: A severity attribute that plausibly predicts/segments resolution time, forming a coherent facet around the focus.

per_column.name: domain_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the technical area of the incident, a natural segmentation dimension for analyzing resolution differences.

per_column.name: recurrence_indicator
per_column.rationale: Captures repeat incidence, an attribute relevant to problem persistence and resolution effort; fits the analytical frame.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on a coherent, data-inferable focus: incident resolution performance and its drivers. resolution_time_hours is the clear central measure, while is_critical, domain_type, and recurrence_indicator act as differentiated predictor/segmentation attributes (severity, technical domain, recurrence) around it -- a sound predictor/outcome structure rather than a single restatement or noise. The focus is genuinely actionable: an analyst can investigate which domains, severities, or recurring incidents drive long resolution times. Minor weakness: recurrence_indicator's semantics are ambiguous (0/1/2/3 with no description) and it leans slightly toward a separate 'recurrence' theme, and the high NULL rate in resolution_time_hours signals derivation issues -- so the set is coherent but not maximally tight, and the exact focus framing (efficiency vs. recurrence) is somewhat mixed.
